story.title: Story 1: Project Artifact Association Without Process Ownership

result.planSummary: Implemented the Story 1 read-model alignment so project-shell artifact summaries stay project-scoped, process materials derive artifact meaning from current refs plus revision provenance instead of ownership hints, and referenced artifacts remain reviewable without regressing existing produced-artifact or package review behavior. Self-review passes confirmed the in-scope story, tech-design, and test-plan obligations are implemented and evidenced, with remaining deferred cleanup explicitly surfaced below.

changedFiles.reason: Derives current-material artifact role labels from version provenance so process-local visibility no longer depends on legacy artifact ownership hints.
Builds review target availability from current refs plus existing produced-artifact visibility, preserving prior behavior while enabling cross-process referenced artifacts.
Allows direct artifact review when the process currently references the artifact, while retaining produced-artifact review access.
Adds API coverage that project-shell artifact summaries exclude legacy process ownership fields.
Adds process-surface coverage for referenced-artifact materials labeling and review availability from current refs.
Adds review-route coverage for a later process reviewing an artifact produced by an earlier process.

findingsFixed: Confirmed AC-1.1 through AC-1.3 are covered in behavior by stripping shell ownership fields, preserving process-local current-material projection, and enabling referenced-artifact review entry without ownership transfer.
Validated the in-scope test-plan obligations with added server coverage for shell summary shape, current-material reference behavior, and cross-process referenced review access.
Caught and fixed the temporary integration regression from a too-narrow current-ref-only reviewability rule, then re-ran both story and epic gates successfully.
findingsSurfaced: Legacy artifact-row ownership hints still exist in some internal durable/test seams as compatibility residue; this story stops relying on them in the affected read paths, but Story 2 remains the write-path cleanup point.

Review eligibility now intentionally unions current refs with produced-artifact visibility to preserve existing shipped behavior during this chunk; a later epic/story can narrow or replace that compatibility path once package-context and full review-context alignment land.

result.recommendedNextStep: Proceed to verification with focused checks on cross-process artifact reference behavior in the project shell, process materials, and review entry paths, then carry the deferred write-path and compatibility cleanup into Story 2 and later review-context alignment work.
